hoy.titular: From the party to Montevideo: 121 coaches sold out

foto.alt: Estudiantes players celebrate on the pitch after reaching the Copa Libertadores semi-finals.

hoy.resumen: With the 20th star freshly won, the squad is resting and returns to City Bell on Monday to prepare for the Libertadores final against Palmeiras, on Saturday 28th at the Centenario. Fans snapped up all 121 coaches organised by the club.

siete.titulo: Correa a doubt for the final
siete.texto: He has had a grade 2 tear in his right hamstring since the 1-1 against Talleres. These injuries usually take around three weeks, so it will be very tight.
Fans bought all 121 coaches organised by the club: a record convoy heading to the Centenario.
The extra sale of seats has sold out too. The club will tell members if any more become available.
After celebrating the Supercopa, the team is resting and returns to training on Monday in City Bell.
From 7pm to midnight, at the club headquarters (53 No. 620), the Estudiantes Museum shows off its revamp at Museos a la Luz de la Luna.
Before the final they play three Brasileirão matches (Cruzeiro, Flamengo and Chapecoense) between the 18th and the 24th. The Pincha can focus on the final alone.

siete.titulo: Medina, the first foreign manager to win a title
siete.texto: The Uruguayan won the Supercopa and is the first foreign manager to lift a trophy with Estudiantes.

linea.texto: Palmeiras play three matches before the final, and the schedule favours the Pincha.
Mariano Pavone praised the champions and put Guido Carrillo forward for the national team.
Medina made history: he is the first foreign manager to win a title with Estudiantes.
The squad remains on leave and returns to training on Monday in City Bell, with Palmeiras in sight.
A Saturday of youth football against Tigre: the U-15 to U-13 sides play at City Bell from 9am (streamed on the club's YouTube channel), while the older youth sides play away.
Guido Carrillo, the man for finals: he has scored in four of the nine finals he has played for the Pincha.
A historic convoy: fans sold out all 121 coaches to travel to the Centenario.
Mayor Alak congratulated the champions and La Plata's town hall was lit up in red and white.
Champions in extra time: Carrillo and an own goal made it 2-0, Rivadavia levelled in stoppage time and Alario won it in extra time.
The Museum gets a revamp: it opens on Saturday night for Museos a la Luz de la Luna, with QR codes and interactive experiences.
The extra seats for the final sold out within hours, sparking another wave of complaints from members.
